subject.title: plugins.entries.<id>.subagent.allowModelOverride is ignored for interactive (client-scoped) subagent runs

question: Should the shipped `plugins.entries.<id>.subagent.allowModelOverride` grant authorize plugin subagent provider/model overrides from interactive client-scoped contexts, and how should plugin HTTP route scopes be treated?
rationale: Current SDK docs and the reported workflow expect the opt-in to authorize subagent model overrides generally, but shipped config help and the candidate PR acknowledge a semantic widening of an existing trust key across an authorization boundary.

options.title: Approve Widened Grant
options.body: Land or revise the linked PR so explicit plugin-scoped subagent trust applies in background and scoped contexts, bounded by `allowedModels` and non-transitive internal authority.

options.title: Narrow Scoped Contexts
options.body: Revise the fix to cover interactive operator-scoped plugin runs while excluding plugin HTTP route scopes if maintainers want that boundary preserved.

options.title: Keep Background-Only
options.body: Reject the runtime behavior change and update SDK docs plus runtime errors so operators know this config key cannot authorize interactive plugin subagent overrides.

recommendation.title: Approve Widened Grant
recommendation.body: Land or revise the linked PR so explicit plugin-scoped subagent trust applies in background and scoped contexts, bounded by `allowedModels` and non-transitive internal authority.

likelyOwner.reason: jalehman has the strongest feature-history signal for the shipped trusted plugin subagent override policy and config-contract decision.
